subject: Network connectivity options for ArgoFin private deployment — VPC Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN
messages:

To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@argofin.com>

Subject: Private deployment — connectivity approach (ArgoFin POC)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team asked for a quick recommendation comparing three connectivity modes for a Private deployment: VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink, and a Site-to-Site VPN. Key constraints:
- Strict egress control (no internet paths from inference nodes)
- Auditability for requests and key material separation
- Low latency for a subset of high-throughput inference calls (~50ms p50 target)
- We expect bursty daytime traffic with occasional large batched evals

Would Redwood be able to outline the tradeoffs and, ideally, a recommended default for our initial POC and a hardened design if we move to production? Also, can you confirm whether PrivateLink supports client IP preservation for our logging needs?

Appreciate a short write-up — Sanjay and our security folks are looped.

Thanks,
Owen

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment — connectivity approach (ArgoFin POC)

Hi Owen — thanks for the clear constraints. Putting a short summary first, then recommended path for POC vs production and a quick ops checklist.

TL;DR recommendations
- POC (fast, low-friction): Site-to-Site VPN (managed) — fastest to stand up, flexible routing, works with your existing on-prem firewalls. Downside: operational overhead and higher latency variability.
- Mid-term (latency + security balance): VPC Peering when your tenant VPCs are in the same cloud and account boundaries allow it — lower latency and simpler path, but no cross-region/global reach and limited traffic controls.
- Production (high-assurance): PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) for control-plane and critical API endpoints + dedicated VPC Peering for bulk KV/cache traffic — hybrid approach that gives strict egress control, stronger isolation, and predictable latency.

Why we suggest hybrid for production
- PrivateLink provides a narrow, controlled endpoint with customer-managed NACLs and easier audit surface for ingress to Redwood services. It also minimizes exposure of IP ranges.
- VPC Peering (or AWS Transit Gateway for multi-VPC scale) is more efficient for high-throughput internal traffic and avoids per-request proxying overhead. Use peering/transit for large model KV cache sync and batching pipelines.

Notes on client IP preservation
- PrivateLink terminates at an ENI in the service provider VPC; native client-source IP is NOT preserved at the application layer across the ENI (you see the ENI IP). For logging, we typically recommend mutual TLS with client certs and adding an application-level header that conveys original client identity (Redwood will sign that header). If IP-level origin is required for compliance, VPC Peering or S2S with source NAT disabled is preferable.

I've attached a short matrix and a draft network diagram. Ben and Kim — please review the matrix and add any infra constraints before I send to ArgoFin's security team.

Next steps
1) Triage matrix w/ infra constraints (internal) — Ben/Kim, 48 hours
2) Send recommended POC design + runbook to Owen & Sanjay — Tessa, 72 hours
3) Setup an ops call with ArgoFin network team to walk through IP allowlists and test plan — schedule after step 2

Thanks,

1) For the hybrid production option you mentioned (PrivateLink for control-plane + peering for bulk traffic) — how do you handle key separation and KMS integration? We need to ensure logs, telemetry, and request traces do not leak PII and that customer keys can be enforced where required.
2) What monitoring we should expect to receive from Redwood (flow logs, VPC Flow, token-level traces)?

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment — connectivity approach (ArgoFin POC)

Hi all — following up with concrete answers and an ops-safe recommendation. Apologies for the slightly long note — wanted to be explicit for procurement and security reviewers.

Short answers to Sanjay's Qs
1) Key separation / KMS: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) with envelope encryption. Control-plane metadata (routing, traces) are stored in Redwood-managed telemetry zones; however, we offer an option to push sensitive traces to your collector via PrivateLink with an encrypted channel. Customer keys can be used for model artifacts and payload encryption at rest. For very sensitive customers we provide an on-prem HSM integration as part of Redwood Private.
2) Monitoring surface: You will get VPC Flow logs (if peering/transit), PrivateLink endpoint metrics (CloudWatch-style), token-level cost/latency traces in the Redwood Console, and optional log-forwarding for request-level traces (via Secure Forwarder over PrivateLink).

Failover and egress guarantees
- Our hybrid production topology can be configured so that fallback pathways also terminate over PrivateLink or peered links; we avoid public internet egress for failover by design. That requires pre-provisioned capacity and routing rules in your VPCs (we'll document exact BGP/route priorities for S2S and Transit Gateway).

Operational checklist (summary)
- POC (S2S VPN): allocate temporary VPN endpoint + route table entries, two test client subnets, basic flow logs enabled. Expect 24–48 hours to validate.
- Production (Hybrid): create PrivateLink endpoints for API ingress; establish peering or Transit Gateway for bulk traffic; configure CMKs + optional HSM, enable flow logs and Secure Forwarder. Allow 2–4 weeks for full hardening depending on procurement.

Attachments and artifacts
- network-diagram-v2.pdf (annotated topology)
- redwood-argo-network-matrix.xlsx (cost/latency matrix)
- runbook stub (we will export as a shared Confluence page once you confirm topology)

I'll pull these into a short confluence page and ping your SREs with a proposed date for a hands-on setup call. If you prefer a single-mode approach for the first quarter, we recommend starting with an S2S VPN to validate traffic and then migrate critical paths to PrivateLink + Peering as you ramp.

Ben Carter
